questions.question: Which club holds the Premier League record for the most consecutive drawn matches in a single season, recording seven straight draws during the autumn of 2009?
questions.explanation: Under Mark Hughes, Manchester City drew seven consecutive league fixtures between September and November 2009, setting a top-flight record.

questions.question: True or False: Fulham's Craven Cottage features the Johnny Haynes Stand, which is officially designated as a Grade II listed structure.
questions.explanation: Designed by celebrated architect Archibald Leitch and opened in 1905, the Johnny Haynes Stand remains the oldest seating structure in English professional football and holds Grade II listed status.
questions.anchorClues: Craven Cottage Johnny Haynes Stand Grade II listed

questions.question: Which Portuguese manager guided Wolverhampton Wanderers to consecutive 7th-place Premier League finishes in 2018–19 and 2019–20 following their promotion from the Championship?
questions.explanation: Nuno Espírito Santo established Wolves as a top-half force immediately upon their return to the top flight, securing European qualification in 2019.
questions.anchorClues: Nuno Espírito Santo / Wolves 7th place finishes

questions.question: In August 2021, Brentford marked their debut match in the Premier League with a famous 2–0 victory over Arsenal at which new home ground?
questions.explanation: Brentford left their historic Griffin Park home in 2020 and opened their top-flight era at the Brentford Community Stadium with an opening-night win against Arsenal.

questions.question: True or False: Peter Crouch holds the record for the most total substitute appearances in Premier League history.
questions.explanation: Peter Crouch held the record with 158 substitute appearances for many years, but James Milner subsequently broke the mark, becoming the first player to surpass 200 appearances off the bench.
questions.anchorClues: James Milner substitute appearances record Premier League

questions.question: Which club staged the greatest comeback in Premier League history by recovering from 4–0 down at half-time to draw 4–4 against Arsenal in February 2011, capped by Cheick Tioté's late volley?
questions.explanation: Newcastle United rallied from 4–0 behind at St James' Park, with Tioté's iconic 87th-minute thunderbolt completing an unprecedented four-goal comeback.

questions.question: Which squad number was worn by English winger Aaron Lennon during his decade at Tottenham Hotspur, during which he made over 260 Premier League appearances for the North London club?
questions.explanation: Aaron Lennon occupied Tottenham Hotspur's number 7 shirt from 2005 through to 2015, becoming a mainstay on the right wing at White Hart Lane.
questions.anchorClues: Aaron Lennon shirt number 7 / Tottenham Hotspur

questions.question: Which Nigerian forward became the first African player to reach 50 Premier League goals, accomplishing the milestone across spells with Arsenal, West Bromwich Albion, and Portsmouth?
questions.explanation: Nwankwo Kanu arrived in the Premier League in 1999 and scored 54 goals across his top-flight career, becoming the first African player to reach the 50-goal milestone.
questions.anchorClues: Nwankwo Kanu 50 Premier League goals African record

questions.question: Which French World Cup winner made over 140 Premier League appearances for Chelsea between 1998 and 2004, serving as club captain prior to John Terry inheriting the armband?
questions.explanation: Marcel Desailly anchored Chelsea's defence for six seasons and captained the side during their transformation into top-four regulars under Claudio Ranieri.

questions.question: Which goalkeeper set the Premier League record for the longest individual run without conceding a goal, keeping 14 consecutive clean sheets (1,311 minutes) during the 2008–09 season?
questions.explanation: Edwin van der Sar went unbeaten for 14 straight Premier League matches for Manchester United between November 2008 and March 2009, setting an all-time top-flight record.
questions.anchorClues: Edwin van der Sar 1,311 minutes clean sheet record
